about: EarthTurn watch face, everything needed to draw it live. All positions and sizes are in the face's 450 x 450 grid (centre 225,225, disc radius 225); multiply by imagePx/450 for the delivered images. Angles are degrees clockwise from straight up, the Watch Face Format convention. Generated by tools/web/EarthTurnWeb.java from the face's own generator code.

projection.type: azimuthal equidistant, North Pole at the centre
projection.radiusOf: r(lat) = (90 - lat) / 150 * 225; latitudes below -60 sit on the rim
projection.point: x = 225 - r * sin(lon), y = 225 - r * cos(lon), lon in degrees east; so longitude 0 is straight up and east runs counter-clockwise in the unrotated map image
projection.mapImageOrientation: map-<style>.png has longitude 0 (Greenwich) straight up; this is the face's rotation zero, which the watch shows at 12:00 UTC

rotation.sign: positive is clockwise; the angle falls through the day, so the map turns counter-clockwise on screen, one turn per day
rotation.rotationOrigin: at 00:00 UTC the angle is 180 and longitude 180 points straight up; at 12:00 UTC it is 0 and Greenwich points up; the numeral a place points at is its local solar hour
rotatesWithMap: date-line label group (the label text is counter-rotated by the same angle so it stays upright)
fixed: night mask (sun at the top, nudged by the equation of time)
date wedge (its start angle moves, see dateLine)

night.images: night-00.png .. night-23.png, black with alpha, sun straight up, alpha 255 where the sun is 12 degrees or more below the horizon, 0 above -0.8 degrees, linear twilight between; tint with the style's night colour and multiply alpha by nightAlpha/255
night.dayOfYearToMaskNote: index d-1 is 1-based day of year d, non-leap year; leap years drift by one day at most
night.equationOfTime: B = rad(360 * (day - 80) / 365); eotMinutes = 9.87 * sin(2B) - 7.53 * cos(B) - 1.5 * sin(B)
night.maskAngleDeg: eotMinutes / 4, clockwise, applied to the mask group about the centre

dateLine.drawn: baked into map-<style>.png: from the pole to the rim along longitude 180, in the style's ink colour, 2.5 wide, dashed 9 on 6 off (grid units)

wedge.meaning: the part of the world on the other date from the wearer's, so the wearer is never inside the tint: before the wearer's midnight it is tomorrow's sector, from the date line clockwise round to midnight at the bottom of the dial; after it, the remainder still on yesterday
wedge.lineAngleDeg: 180 - ((360 * utcMinutesOfDay / 1440 + 180) mod 360)   (where the date line points, clockwise from up, in (-180, 180])
wedge.outsideShape: wearer outside (inWedge false): filled sector of the whole disc from lineAngleDeg clockwise to 180
wedge.insideShape: wearer inside (inWedge true): filled sector from 180 clockwise round to lineAngleDeg + 360 (the rest of the disc)
wedge.inWedge: floor((utcMs + 720 * 60000) / 86400000) == floor((utcMs + localOffsetMinutes * 60000) / 86400000), the same rule as the label
wedge.shownWhen: datechange setting is 'labels' (default) or 'tint'; hidden for 'line'

label.text: '+1d' while the wearer is outside the wedge (before local midnight), '-1d' once inside it
label.rule: inWedge = floor((utcMs + 720 * 60000) / 86400000) == floor((utcMs + localOffsetMinutes * 60000) / 86400000); '-1d' when true, '+1d' otherwise
label.placement: 70 x 32 box centred 165 from the disc centre, in the rotating map frame: at 192 degrees (12 clockwise of the line, inside the wedge) for +1d, at 168 degrees for -1d; the box is counter-rotated so the text stays upright
label.innerWhen: utcMinutesOfDay between 540 and 900 inclusive (09:00 to 15:00 UTC), when the date line points into the bottom sector between the 21 and the 3 where the zone blocks sit
label.topWhen: utcMinutesOfDay 180 or less, or 1260 or more (21:00 to 03:00 UTC), when the date line points into the top sector between the 9 and the 15 over the time block; the label then sits just under the date
label.outline: eight copies in the style's paper colour at offsets (-2,0) (2,0) (0,-2) (0,2) (-1,-1) (1,-1) (-1,1) (1,1) under the label, like the time block

numerals.angleDeg: 180 - h * 15 (so 6 is at the right, 12 at the top, 18 at the left, 24 at the bottom: the ring runs counter-clockwise like the map)
numerals.font: Barlow Bold, 30 for 6/12/18/24, 26 for 3/9/15/21, 22 for the rest, centred in the box
numerals.outline: two copies in the paper colour offset (-1,-1) and (+1,+1) under the numeral
numerals.shown: 3..21 always; 22, 23, 1, 2 when one zone is at the bottom; 24 instead when two zones are

pointer.meaning: a short radial stroke just inside the numerals at the wearer's own hour
pointer.line: from (225, 49) to (225, 37) before rotation, 6 wide, round caps, in the style's ink colour
pointer.image: pointer-<style>.png, full frame at the 12 o'clock position

timeBlock.outline: every line is drawn eight times in the paper colour at offsets (-2,0) (2,0) (0,-2) (0,2) (-1,-1) (1,-1) (-1,1) (1,1), then once in ink on top

time.format: ICU 'h:mm' in 12-hour mode (gives '9:30 AM'), 'HH:mm' in 24-hour mode

date.format: ICU 'EEE d MMM' (gives 'Wed 9 Sep'; the watch localises)

battery.rule: '<n>%' in batteryRed at 15% and below, '100%' in batteryAmber when full, nothing otherwise

zoneBlocks.colours: both styles use the vintage ink and paper here: ink #3B3220, outline #F1E6C8
zoneBlocks.outline: four copies in the paper colour at (-2,0) (2,0) (0,-2) (0,2) under the ink for the hour and name; two at (-1,-1) (1,1) for the day marker
zoneBlocks.hour: the zone's 24-hour hour, two digits, ICU 'HH'
zoneBlocks.dayMarker: '+1d' when the zone's calendar date is ahead of the wearer's, '-1d' when behind, else nothing: floor((utcMs + zoneOffsetMin * 60000) / 86400000) - floor((utcMs + localOffsetMin * 60000) / 86400000)
zoneBlocks.minuteMarker: '+30m', '+45m' or '+15m' after the name when ((zoneOffsetMin - localOffsetMin) mod 60) is 30, 45 or 15, else nothing
zoneBlocks.name: the zone id in upper case (DEN, PPG), then a space and the minute marker
zoneBlocks.layoutRule: Zone 2 off: Zone 1 in the single block; Zone 2 on: Zone 1 left, Zone 2 right in the pair boxes

cityDots.shape: 14 px disc in the paper colour #F1E6C8 with a 10 px disc in dotRed on top, centred on the projected city, in the rotating map frame

fonts.sizes: font sizes above are the face's pixel sizes in the 450 grid

ambient: in ambient mode the watch shows the dark style with no dots, no wedge, no label and no zone blocks; not needed on the web
renderChecklist: Draw the date-line label (dateLine.label): a red '+1d' or '-1d' in Barlow Bold 26 with the paper outline beside the date line, in the rotating map frame at 192 or 168 degrees, at radius 165, or 105 during innerWhen, or 50 during topWhen, counter-rotated to stay upright. It is shown whenever the datechange setting is 'labels' (the default), which is the setting the reference captures use.
Format the time and date with the en-US locale, as the watch does: ICU 'h:mm a' gives '5:46 AM' (no leading zero, AM/PM), 'EEE, MMM d' gives 'Wed, Sep 9'. Not the en-GB forms '5:46' and 'Wed 2 Sept'.
Tint the other-date side (dateLine.wedge): outsideShape when inWedge is false, insideShape when it is true; the wearer's own place is never inside the tint.
